# Paired horizontal and rotated font-size control

`font-sizes.docx` is an original eight-page control generated by
`tools/cell_text_direction_font_sizes_fixture.py`. Each page contains the same
centered Arial text in horizontal, bottom-to-top and top-to-bottom cells. Sizes
are 8, 8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11 and 12pt. Rows have exact heights, symmetric
margins and exact paragraph spacing. Compatibility mode is 15.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.72 (`textDirection`), 17.3.2.38 (`sz`) and
17.3.1.13 (`jc`) describe the source properties. This control isolates text
placement; it does not establish automatic row sizing, nested-table origins,
arbitrary fonts or automatic line leading.

The reference application exports eight pages. PDF font sizes are quantized (for example,
8pt is reported as 8.04pt), but this is not evidence that layout must measure
the source at that quantized size. All 24 browser text origins agree with the
native PDF within 0.104pt. Horizontal and rotated samples retain the existing
0.15pt X / 0.2pt Y test tolerances. Both sets of four-page comparison sheets
were inspected. No rotation-specific offset or font-size change is warranted
by this control.

The source and three browser exports pass all 12 XML-part schema checks.
No-edit package equality, insertion, unrelated-part preservation, exact undo
and edited reopening pass. The first scratch version placed `tblBorders`
after `tblLayout`; schema validation caught that ordering error. The committed
source fixes the order, and its native reference PDF and browser exports were regenerated.
The JSON reference binds this corrected source and native PDF by SHA-256.

Regenerate from the repository root:

```powershell
python tools/cell_text_direction_font_sizes_fixture.py
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/export-reference.ps1 -SourceFullPath "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/font-sizes.docx" -OutputPdf "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/font-sizes-native.pdf"
python tools/record_cell_text_direction.py font-sizes
```

This investigation was prompted by corpus document #338. A fresh 15-page export
reproduces its existing maximum reading-axis difference of 0.213862pt. Its
measured first-ticket row-border centers differ by less than 0.1pt. The simple
control does not reproduce that larger residual, so the original remains
partial. It must not be classified as an automatic rotated-baseline defect
based only on that reading-axis difference. No production behavior changed.
